title: Trade pounds with a liquidity pool
summary: Alice deposits 100,000 GBP and 127,000 USD in a pool; Bob swaps 1,000 GBP for dollars at the pool's price, and the fee makes the pool grow.

steps.title: Make Alice
steps.text: Every action on a blockchain is signed by a key. This step creates Alice's key, which is how she proves she is Alice.

steps.title: Make Bob
steps.text: Bob gets his own key too, so he can act separately from Alice.

steps.title: Start a chain
steps.text: A chain is a private practice network, like a sandbox. This makes a fresh one and gives Alice and Bob some of its native coin to pay fees.

steps.title: Create the pound token
steps.text: A token is a made-up currency tracked by a program on the chain. Alice creates pounds (GBP, two decimal places) and receives all one million of them.

steps.title: Create the dollar token
steps.text: Alice also creates dollars (USD, six decimal places) and receives all one million of them, so she holds both sides of the market.

steps.title: Alice sends Bob 1,000 pounds
steps.text: Sending tokens is the simplest transaction: Alice moves 1,000 of her pounds to Bob, so he has something to trade.

steps.title: Put up a pool
steps.text: A pool is a program that holds two tokens and trades between them at a price set by how much of each it holds. Alice puts one on the chain for pounds and dollars.

steps.title: Alice allows the pool to move her pounds
steps.text: Before a program can move your tokens, you must say it may, and how many. Alice allows the pool to take the pounds her deposit needs.

steps.title: Alice allows the pool to move her dollars
steps.text: The deposit needs dollars too, so Alice gives the same permission for what the add needs in dollars.

steps.title: Alice fills the pool: 100,000 pounds and 127,000 dollars
steps.text: The first deposit sets the price: 127,000 dollars for 100,000 pounds is 1.27 dollars a pound. Alice gets shares in the pool in return, her claim on what it holds.

steps.title: Bob allows the pool to move his pounds
steps.text: Bob will pay the pool in pounds, so he allows it to take what the swap needs.

steps.title: Bob swaps 1,000 pounds for dollars
steps.text: Bob pays 1,000 pounds and the pool pays dollars at its price, less a 0.3% fee that stays in the pool for Alice. He accepts at most 0.5% less than the quote; if someone traded first and moved the price further, the swap would refuse.

steps.title: See the pool
steps.text: Here is the pool now: more pounds, fewer dollars, a slightly lower price for pounds, and k a little bigger: the fee stayed in the pool.
